prospect.name: Chase R
prospect.location: Bentonville, Northwest Arkansas, USA — recently relocated from Northwest Louisiana
prospect.occupation: Branch manager of a roofing company, running a newly opened branch. On a $75,000 base salary with 1099 commission bonuses on top. Previously a petroleum geologist. Spends the day climbing roofs, walking neighbourhoods and door-knocking, plus significant driving between sites.
prospect.family_status: Married with a two-year-old, a three-year-old and a nine-year-old stepson. Family has not yet relocated to Arkansas — they move up in about a month. He and his wife are several weeks into an ongoing argument. Wife does not work outside the home and manages the household budget; the family is re-budgeting for private school.
prospect.training_background: Wrestled and powerlifted through high school and stayed in the gym until roughly 25, then moved into corporate work and stopped. Has not lifted consecutively in a long time. Trained legs at a gym the day before this call for the first time in ages. Tried jiu-jitsu briefly and stopped after a training partner injured a knee. Now plays golf as a low-impact alternative and has walked 18 holes recently. Stays incidentally active through roof climbing and door-knocking. Bought roughly $1,000 of home gym equipment two years ago, never used it, and eventually sold it.
prospect.medical: Volunteered a family history of cardiac death — 'there may or may not be some kind of hereditary heart issues in our family. I've had an uncle that passed from a heart attack and his father as well' — which the rep did not respond to. A recurring right knee problem that tightens and stops him running, and which recurred walking downhill on a golf course. Sciatic symptoms that have started flaring from prolonged sitting and driving. Otherwise reports no long-term injuries. No health-conditions question was asked at any point on the call.

notable.note: Best objection-handling call in the batch on money and the worst on urgency. The rep isolated cleanly, asked the monthly surplus question and the credit score, and then — asked point blank for the lowest number the company would accept — refused to name one and answered with structure instead. That is a clean price hold and the direct opposite of what the same rep did on the Chris Wiley and Bennu calls. But the prospect handed him a textbook not-the-right-time objection along with the reason it mattered — 'I don't want to lose the fire that I have right now' — and no part of that play ran; the August 17 date was accepted on first offer, three weeks after the spark. Clinically, the prospect volunteered a family history of premature cardiac death, an uncle and that uncle's father both from heart attacks, and the rep did not acknowledge it at all before selling high-intensity conditioning. The hip-dysplasia and declined-hip-replacement anecdote appears here for the third time in this batch, and this time it is followed by the rep offering a mechanism for the prospect's knee problem and dismissing ankle-support footwear as 'total BS'.
